div.head: Protocol description
div.p: In this protocol, the token contains a priority field which replates node's access to the ring. The value of this pnority field indicates the service priority level. Every frame (token and data) also contain a priority reservation field. Each node examines the priority reservation field in frame header as a frame passes b A node overwrites the contents of the reservation fie6 by inserting the highest priority of its pending mes sages (if any) if and only if this priority is higher than the one current1 present in this field. This enables the reservation .$eld .to represent the highest priorit of messages wmtmg in the system. The station h o d ing the token can transmit till its token holding timer expires after which it releases a free token having a rionty equal to the known highest priorit of en& messages. A node is allowed to capture t i e d e n and transmit its messages only when it has higher priority messages pending compared to the token priority. The reader is referred to [7, 211 for further details on the protocol operation.

div.head: Protocol parameter settings

div.head: Assignment of Message P r i o n t k s
div.p: In order to guarantee their deadlines, the messages must be assigned priorities in a proper manner. This problem is similar to the problem of at+ signing pnorities to periodic tasks in the context of cpu scheduling. It is well known that the rote monotonic algorithm [12], which assigns higher priorities to tasks with shorter periods, is the o p timal static priority, greemptive cpu schedulin algorithm for this pro lem. Further, as was firif proposed by Strosnider in [22], this algorithm can be applied to token rings. Thus the synchronous messages are assi ed priorities in the inverse order of their periog.

div.head: Choice of h m e Size
div.p: The rate monotonic algorithm requires that a node with a high priority message be able to preempt the transmission by a node yith a lower priority message. Since the transmssion of a lower riority message cannot be arbitrarily preempted gy the arrival of a higher priority me+ge, preemption is only approximated by dividing messages into frames. The individual stations contend for the right to transmit a frame by using the reservation field of the frame header. Hence preemption can take glace only after the transmitting station receives ack the header of the transmtted frame and knows the highest priority claim by other stations on the ring. A small frame size provides a better approximation of the preemption requirement. However, there are k e d overheads associated with the transmission of each frame. div.head: Conclusions
div.p: The schedulability conditions for the timed token protocol and the priority driven protocol (implementing a rate monotonic scheduling policy) were developed. These criteria were then used to study the average case behavior of the two rotowls by estimating their average breakdown utiLation values. Our studies have shown that neither protocol is ideal for real-time mm munications over the entire range of network operating oonditions. The priority driven protocol can be used to implement optimal scheduling policy such as the rate monotonic algorithm. At low transmission speeds (1-10 Mbps), this implementation is very efficient. The timed token rotocol essentially implements a round robin schedufng policy without any priority arbitration mechanism. At low transmission speeds, the riority inversions caused by such a round robin sche8uling approach tend to adversely affect the messages with short deadlines. Thus at low transmission speeds the priority driven protocol is better suited for real-time applications than the timed token protocol. The riority arbitration overheads incurred b the riority h v e n protowl increase mth network ban&"& thereby lowering the performance of the priority driven protocol for high speed networks. The. timed token protocol which does not incur priority arbitratlon overheads and allows multi le kames to be on the ring at the.same time is founcfto perform better at high bandwdths such as 100 Mbps and above.
